title: experiment: fast quant scheduler to reduce short-sequence latency
author: Avery Patel
description:
Context: This PR adds an experimental scheduler that preferentially routes short-sequence requests to a low-latency path optimized for quantized kernels. Motivation: many interactive workloads (chat boxes, search snippets) have short generation lengths where kernel launch and scheduling overheads dominate. This experiment attempts to reduce median and tail latency by introducing a lightweight fast-quant execution path and a request classifier that routes <128-token sequences to the fast path when feature flag is enabled.

What this contains: single continuous description string. Implementation details: new scheduler module (runtime/fast_quant_scheduler.py), a small request classifier that uses token-length + model-profile heuristics, lightweight kernel selection hints for the runtime, and a toggleable config flag (runtime.features.fast_quant_scheduler=true). Benchmarks are included in the PR body.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p4d-8x using the bert-600 and opt-125m variants show median token latency improvement of ~18-22% for sequences <=64 tokens, p95 improvement of ~12%. End-to-end chat simulation with gallery prompts shows ~14% median latency win and negligible quality regressions on sampled outputs.

Safety and risk: this is an experiment. Fast path uses a more aggressive quantized kernel which may yield slightly different float outputs; we recommend enabling only for non-critical customers while we run regression suites. The scheduler is feature-flag guarded and defaults to off. We added a rollout plan in the checklist.

How to test locally: run `pytest tests/runtime/test_fast_quant_scheduler.py` and `scripts/bench/compare_latency.sh --model opt-125m --seq 32,64 --runs 1000`. There is also a small CLI `tools/ff_scheduler_ctl.py` to toggle the flag on local dev clusters.

Notes: this PR is intentionally self-contained with clear toggles and metrics so it can be A/Bed and iterated quickly.
